Attack the SMALL shapes shape0 (n32 B20, 10us), shape1 (n176 B40, 278us), shape2 (n352 B40, 736us) -- each weighs as much in the geomean as a huge shape, and they are launch/latency-bound at tiny batch, not compute-bound. Build a SINGLE persistent megakernel that factors the entire small batch with ZERO host round-trips and ZERO per-step kernel launches: one grid-resident kernel doing the whole blocked QR for n<=352, or a cudaGraph-style fixed replay (NO CUDA streams -- the remote rejects stream APIs). The current path issues many small launches whose overhead dominates at this size. Even a 2x on these three multiplies into the geomean. Validate HARD (these are well-conditioned cond1); interleaved A/B; profile in isolation. NEVER use 'timeout' or any shell-timeout wrapper -- the harness auto-backgrounds long commands.

Unblocked whole-matrix smem megakernel for n=176 (one CTA/matrix, whole matrix in 124KB smem, deep-pipeline 1-sync Householder over all 176 cols, zero per-step launches). Validates all 21 shapes. REGRESSION on n=176: 277->525us (1.9x slower) -- the 176-deep sync chain + shrinking per-col parallelism beats the host blocked path's batched cuBLAS trailing GEMMs. n=352 unchanged (megakernel OFF, won't fit smem). geomean 2045.5 vs 1936.7 baseline. Next: block the megakernel (short panel chains + one wide in-smem WY trailing apply per panel).

Blocked in-smem WY megakernel for n=176 (PB=32, wide trailing W=VtC/X=TtW/C-=VX in smem). Fixed smem undercount (illegal access) + T->Tt in trailing (Q_panel^T). Validates all 21 (n=176 scaled_factor_resid 0.035, orth 0.57). REGRESSION: n=176 277->1112us (4x). KEY FINDING: a single CTA/matrix doing in-smem scalar-FMA matmuls at B=40 (40 CTAs/148 SMs) can't match cuBLAS device-wide batched tensor GEMMs; the host path's launches are NOT the bottleneck, GPU GEMM throughput is. Megakernel is a dead end here. geomean 2176 vs 1936.7. Next: profile baseline n=176 in isolation to find the real lever (likely the panel kernel or build_Minv, not launches).

Force TF32 tensor-op trailing GEMMs for n=176 (GemmEx COMPUTE_32F_FAST_TF32) + megakernel OFF. CLEAN isolation profile (no checker) of n=176 custom_kernel: PANEL kernel 71%, build_Minv 14.6%, trailing GEMMs ~14%. force_top makes the trailing GEMMs run cutlass_80_tensorop_s1688gemm (TF32 tensor cores) vs simt_sgemm, but they're only 14% so win is in noise: n=176 277.86 vs 277.35us, geomean 1933.8 vs 1936.7. KEY FINDING: n=176 is PANEL-KERNEL-bound (59.7us/panel x3 panels), NOT launch/GEMM-bound -- the brief's megakernel premise is wrong here. Next: attack the panel via two-level (short inner chain) or CholeskyQR2 (GEMM-bound, no serial Householder chain).

Tiny-shape dispatch fast-path: hoist n<=32 out of the _arms lambda-tuple so shape0 skips per-call closure allocs. NEUTRAL: the harness CUDA-event-times around the kernel, so host-Python dispatch is outside the timed region; shape0 stays 10.28us (GPU+launch floor). Final clean isolation profile (no checker) of n=176: PANEL 71%, build_Minv 14.6%, trailing GEMMs ~14% (now all cutlass tensor-op s1688gemm via force_top). Path confirmed at its tuned local optimum. Validates all 21, geomean 1933.5-1936.2 == baseline 1936.7.

Brief exhausted; best geomean 1933.5us == baseline 1936.7us (no net improvement, no regression; safe committed state at 12d8de9). KEY FINDING that overturns the brief's premise: clean ISOLATION profiling (no checker) shows n=176/352 are NOT launch-bound -- they are PANEL-KERNEL-COMPUTE-bound (panel = 71% of n=176, 69% of n=352 GPU-active time; build_Minv ~15-18%; trailing GEMMs only ~14% and already tensor-op). The serial Householder panel chain underutilizes the device at B=40 (only 40 CTAs / 148 SMs) but is stall-bound, not gap-bound. Things TRIED and their results: (1) whole-matrix smem megakernel, unblocked: REGRESSED 277->525us (n-deep sync chain); (2) blocked in-smem WY megakernel: REGRESSED 277->1112us (single CTA's in-smem scalar matmuls can't match cuBLAS device-wide batched GEMMs) -- megakernel is a confirmed dead-end here, GPU-compute-bound not launch-bound; (3) CholeskyQR2: REGRESSED 822us AND numerically unstable (Gram A^T A not positive-definite even at cond=1 in FP32/TF32, needs FP64 Gram); (4) two-level for n=176: REGRESSED 514-671us; (5) force TF32 tensor-op trailing GEMMs (GemmEx COMPUTE_32F_FAST_TF32): NEUTRAL but correct (kept ON -- GEMMs now run cutlass tensor-op s1688gemm vs simt_sgemm, but they're only ~14% so win is in noise); (6) block sweep n=176 (30/44/60/88/176): block=60 already optimal; (7) n=352 bf16 OB/IB/warps/blk4 sweep: current config already optimal; (8) tiny-shape Python dispatch fast-path: NEUTRAL (harness CUDA-event-times the kernel, host-Python is outside the timed region; shape0 stuck at GPU+launch-latency floor 10.3us). CONCLUSION: shapes 0/1/2 are at their tuned local optima from prior workers; the panel is the irreducible bottleneck given single-CTA-per-matrix at B=40. SUGGESTIONS for the next brief: the ONLY untried lever with potential upside is a MULTI-CTA ROW-COOPERATIVE panel (split the m-row reductions across P CTAs to fill the idle ~108 SMs) -- the existing msplit machinery is build-light-pruned and bf16/two-level-entangled, so it would need a fresh clean impl; but expected payoff is low for n=176 (small m=176 -> per-column reduction too small to outweigh the cross-CTA barrier cost) and only marginal for n=352 (m=352). A better use of effort is the LARGE shapes (3,4,5,6,7) where absolute time dominates. Megakernel and CholeskyQR2 lines for n<=352 should NOT be re-explored -- both are measured dead-ends.

Conversely torch wins n352 (cuSOLVER-loop 51K vs cuBLAS 129K) and n>=1024 (vastly). So the optimal LIBRARY routing: n512->cuBLAS-batched, else torch.geqrf. Next iteration: implement that per-n routing.

v3 OPTIMAL LIBRARY ROUTING: cuBLAS geqrfBatched for n in {32,512}, torch.geqrf for n in {176,352,1024,2048,4096}. Validates all 22. geomean=104908us (best clean-library result; 20% better than v2 hybrid 132052; vs mature 1935 = 54x). PER-SHAPE (us): s0=334(cuBLAS), s1=20025(torch), s2=51571(torch), s3 n512B640=539711(cuBLAS, was 1077K via torch -- 2x WIN), s4=243695(torch), s5=77519(torch), s6=54352(torch), s7=539024(cuBLAS), s8=243483(torch), s9=538933(cuBLAS), s10=538983(cuBLAS), s11=243686(torch). The n512 B640 shapes (s3/7/9/10) dropped from ~1077K to ~539K by routing to cuBLAS batched. Clean & readable (~95 lines). Geomean now dominated by n512(539K x4) + n1024(243K x3). Next: attack n512 with a clean blocked compact-WY batched QR (custom panel kernel + cublasSgemmStridedBatched TF32 trailing) -- the cuSOLVER/cuBLAS library calls are the floor for library-only; a tensor-core blocked path can go lower.

v4 BLOCKED compact-WY QR for n=512 (custom batched panel kernel sgeqr2 in smem, PB=32, + cublasSgemmStridedBatched TF32 trailing). Builds, PASSES n512 DENSE + all n!=512 shapes, but FAILS ill-conditioned n512: test.11 n512 nearcollinear scaled_factor_resid=5.51 (>1.0), test.19 n512 mixed scaled=30.1. ROOT CAUSE: CUBLAS_TF32_TENSOR_OP_MATH trailing GEMMs lose precision; fine for well-conditioned but the nearcollinear/mixed-ill-conditioned n512 cases need full FP32 mantissa. The panel kernel itself is CORRECT (dense n512 passes at resid 0.003). Fix next: switch trailing GEMMs to FP32 (CUBLAS_DEFAULT_MATH / disable TF32).

v5 BLOCKED QR with FP32 trailing (CUBLAS_DEFAULT_MATH). VALIDATION (n512 B16) now PASSES incl nearcollinear (resid 0.025) and mixed (0.049). But BENCHMARK FAILS at n512 B640: benchmark.3 (DENSE cond2!) matrix=417 resid=10.3 scaled=399, b.7 mat600 scaled=91, b.9 mat329 scaled=505, b.10 mat367 scaled=670. Fails at SPECIFIC matrices out of 640, even on WELL-CONDITIONED dense -- so this is a BATCH-SIZE-dependent BUG (race/uninit), not pure conditioning (test B16 dense+illcond all pass). Suspect: panel kernel correctness at B=640 (smem 65KB/CTA, 3 CTAs/SM) or strided-GEMM indexing. Next: standalone probe blocked_qr vs torch.geqrf at B=640 to localize the error.

v6 CLEAN BLOCKED compact-WY batched QR for n=512 (custom batched panel kernel: sgeqr2 in smem, PB=32, larfg+batched-larf; trailing update = 3x cublasSgemmStridedBatched FP32). Validates ALL 22. geomean=76583us (27% better than v3 104908; vs mature 1935 = 40x). BIG n512 WIN: s3 n512B640=214608 (was 539711 cuBLAS / 1077168 torch -> 2.5x faster than the best LIBRARY call, 5x vs torch!), s7=209790, s9=199582, s10=214537 (all ~2.5x vs cuBLAS). TWO BUGS FOUND+FIXED: (1) TF32 trailing fails ill-conditioned n512 (nearcollinear/mixed) -> use FP32 (CUBLAS_DEFAULT_MATH); (2) at B>=417 (3 CTAs/SM) the 65KB dynamic-smem panel OVER-SUBSCRIBES the SM -> non-deterministic corruption of random matrices; FIXED by padding dynamic-smem request to 96KB so floor(228/96)=2 CTAs/SM. This proves a CLEAN tensor-core blocked path beats the cuSOLVER/cuBLAS library FLOOR. Geomean now dominated by n1024 (243K x3) + n512 (214K x4). Next: route n1024 to the blocked path too.

v7 route n=1024 to the blocked path as well. Validates all 22. geomean=76613us == v6 76583 (NEUTRAL, within noise). n1024 blocked: s4=243347, s8=243336, s11=243393 -- essentially IDENTICAL to torch.geqrf (243695). The blocked path's 2.5x win at n512 came from B=640 filling the device. So n1024 stays best on torch.geqrf (same speed, simpler). Will revert n1024 to torch. Geomean floor for this clean approach ~76.6K, dominated by n512(214K x4)+n1024(243K x3); both ~40x off mature 1935 (the mature kernel is hyper-tuned and unbeatable by a clean library/blocked path).

v8 parallelize form-T dot products across threads (was O(pb^2*m) serial on tid0, suspected bottleneck) + reverted n1024 to torch. Will probe to localize, then either fix the form-T sync or move V^T V to a batched GEMM outside the kernel.

FRESH-SLATE library/blocked QR done. Best=18905us at commit 2f69408c (clean ~234-line submission, branched off main 58e8bfd7). vs mature 1935=9.76x; but 5.5x BETTER than the best pure-LIBRARY routing (104908) and 35x better than cuBLAS-everywhere (669246). KEY LIBRARY FINDINGS: (1) cublasSgeqrfBatched emits the compact (H,tau) contract natively in ONE call, but is COMPETITIVE only at tiny n -- CATASTROPHIC at large n (n4096=129 SECONDS; it serializes the batch, no blocking/tensor-cores). (2) torch.geqrf routes n<=256 to cublasSgeqrfBatched and n>256 to a cuSOLVER per-matrix LOOP; at n512 B640 the cuBLAS batched call is 2x FASTER than torch's 640-serial-geqrf loop (torch's heuristic is suboptimal there). (3) cuSOLVER has NO batched geqrf. THE WIN: a CLEAN BLOCKED compact-WY batched QR -- custom batched panel kernel (one CTA/matrix, sgeqr2 in smem, emits LAPACK (H,tau) directly, runtime panel width) + cublasSgemmStridedBatched FP32 trailing -- BEATS BOTH LIBRARIES on every n<=1024: 9x@n176, 7x@n352, 16x@n512(vs cuBLAS), 3.8x@n1024(vs torch). PER-SHAPE WINS vs baseline-library: blocked wins shapes 0,1,2,3,4,7,8,9,10,11 (n<=1024); torch.geqrf retained for shapes 5(n2048 B8),6(n4096 B2) where one-CTA-per-matrix underfills 148 SMs. TWO BUGS FOUND+FIXED via compute-sanitizer: (a) a shared-memory Read/Write RACE in the panel kernel (all threads read P[j,c] for w, tid0 writes it) -- benign at low occupancy, corrupted RANDOM matrices at B>~417; one __syncthreads() fixed it. (b) single-pass TF32 trailing FAILS factor_rtol broadly. REMAINING HEADROOM (next brief): the trailing GEMMs are ~47% of GPU time on SIMT FP32 (NOT tensor cores) -- engaging tensor cores needs error-corrected 3xTF32 emulation (split operands hi/lo TF32, sum 3 TF32 GEMMs); could ~halve the n512/n1024 cost but risks ill-conditioned accuracy + C-split overhead. Also: n2048/n4096 need MULTI-CTA-per-matrix to fill the device at B=8/2. This clean blocked path is a strong diversity hedge -- a fundamentally different, readable shape from the mature kernel that decisively beats every stock library call where the batch fills the device.

Single-launch in-smem megakernel for small n (route n<=232 to it; n32 & n176). One CTA/matrix loads whole nxn matrix into smem (col-major), runs full unblocked Householder QR there, writes (H,tau) row-major DIRECTLY to a separate output buffer -- NO host transposes, NO per-panel launches, NO cuBLAS. Trailing update = one-thread-per-trailing-column (no block sync in the apply); only the per-column reflector norm uses a warp+block reduction. BUG FOUND+FIXED: first version overwrote input A in place -> benchmark recheck (which reuses the same input tensor across timed repeats) saw corrupted input and failed with huge residuals; fixed by writing H to a separate empty_like buffer. Validates ALL 22. geomean 18937->16882 (10.8%). PER-SHAPE: s0 n32 226.97->73.82 (3.1x), s1 n176 2254->1762.8 (1.3x), s2 n352 6998 (unchanged, blocked), s3-11 unchanged. vs MATURE: n32 still 7.4x off (10us), n176 6.3x off (278us). Next: cut the per-column block-sync count + improve trailing parallelism; tackle n352.
